Answer: A great deal of the answer is provided in the question.  The answer is simply that you should \strong{love}.  This is true of any of life's quandaries, as there is an old saying: \em{Love is the Answer; Ask the Question again later.}

This doesn't mean that a simple platitude of love is a good answer.  There are many ways to love, and no one loves the same way.  Even if I try to love the same way as you, I will fail in a different way.  One of the best ways to love is to try to understand how you love.  Do you love by sacrificing yourself?  Do you love by seeking love?  Do you love through friendship?  Do you love through sex?  Are there things you hate about the person you love, and if so, how do you love despite them?  Do you love despite having had a traumatic experience of love?

Knowing what you love about your loved one, and why you love them, is the best way to begin loving them.  Doing so can help you with the next question, how to do you love them?

Answer: For what it's worth, my interpretation is that the cyborgs can't love because they can't be truly themselves. They are machines with consciousness, but they don't have a soul or the emotional capacity to love as people do. In order to be human, they must either replace themselves with a human, as in the case of the loom, or they must be in a position where they cannot truly exist, like the cyborg who is the father of the loom, and in which case there's nothing to love.

Answer: I think the answer is that they can’t truly love because they don’t have a soul (of course that’s not going to be the direct answer).  So I think that the cyborgs have to replace themselves with a soul before they can love.  I think the loom does this by taking a part of itself and putting it into a human’s body.
